contexts.text: In truths is the guest-chamber of good.

General notions precede, without which singulars have no lodging to enter into. In a lodging where there are mere shades they do not appear; and in a lodging where there are falsities, they are either rejected, suffocated, or perverted...
For in good all truths are received as guests.
Unless the Natural... becomes nothing, good... has no guest-chamber, but is dissipated.
Evil cannot be received as a guest in Heaven.
Such are at first in a lodging of the vile... and the lodging was seen.
